A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FastVID with the same core pipeline and overlapping experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2's added appendix was also inspected.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original benchmark evaluations and component and hyperparameter ablations on LLaVA-OneVision and LLaVA-Video.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original benchmark, latency, ablation, and qualitative results, including added Qwen2-VL evaluations.

M1.justification: The core DySeg, DTM, and ATS pipeline remains. v2 adds an evaluated FastVID+FastV variant with further pruning at LLM layer 10, extending the original input-pruning procedure without replacing its components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MVBench, LongVideoBench, MLVU, and VideoMME without subtitles. The added Qwen2-VL experiment uses the existing VideoMME task; its different architecture, frame count, and resolution handling change experimental settings rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Input-only PruneVID is renamed PruneVID*, but its OneVision comparisons at 25%, 20%, and 15% retention and both LLaVA-Video comparisons are removed. v2 adds full input-plus-layer-10 PruneVID to the OneVision comparison. This substantially revises evaluation of the principal video-pruning competitor; other baseline families remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces visual-token FLOPs and A100 prefilling-latency evaluation, Qwen2-VL testing with 768 sampled frames and dynamic resolution, controlled newline-retention variants, and two-stage pruning comparisons. These substantially extend the evaluation design beyond v1's accuracy-versus-retention comparisons.

E4.justification: v2 adds a newline-retention control through FastVID* and qualitative token-merging analyses in Figure 5 and Figures 8–10. Existing segmentation, merging, component, and hyperparameter ablations remain; the hyperparameter studies move to Appendix B rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Shared FastVID accuracy scores remain unchanged. New results include FastVID versus vanilla prefilling latency of 67.2 versus 476.3 ms in Table 3 and Qwen2-VL VideoMME accuracy of 60.6 versus 63.0 in Table 7. v2 also adds FLOPs and variant results, replaces near-10% PruneVID results under its reported settings, and removes other PruneVID rows and LLaVA-Video medium-subset scores.

T1.justification: Equation 4 reverses the density inequality from rho_i > rho_j to rho_j > rho_i, correcting the definition to match both versions' higher-density-neighbor explanation. Section 3.3 also changes the anchor-frame count from floor(f/p) to ceil(P/p). These are mathematical corrections, not merely notation changes.

C1.justification: The central context-preserving pruning, accuracy, and generalization claims remain. The abstract and introduction refine the headline from 90% to 90.3% token removal and add explicit claims of 8.3% remaining FLOPs and 7.1-fold prefilling acceleration while retaining 98.0% accuracy.

C2.justification: v1 attributes weaker LLaVA-Video performance retention to stronger per-frame pooling. Appendix C.1 broadens the hypothesis to extensively sampled videos and identifies query-agnostic pruning's risk of missing sparse query-relevant information. v2 also adds substantive interpretations of ATS/DTM visualizations and compression latency.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds substantial baseline reproduction information, including FastV's layer setting, VisionZip's 54:10 token allocation, PruneVID parameters, repository and license information, and FLOP accounting. A100 hardware and additional implementation details are disclosed. FastVID's own code link was already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds FrameFusion, PyramidDrop, grouped-query attention, and the Qwen2 technical report. Related work shifts criticism of video-pruning approaches toward latency and extreme-compression limitations, while retaining the central research positioning. Publication and venue updates to existing references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the introduction and portions of related work and results, clarifies token-allocation explanations, and moves existing hyperparameter discussions into Appendix B. The principal section order and much of the methodology and ablation prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figures 1 and 4 are rearranged, the original combined benchmark table is split and restructured with computational-cost columns, and efficiency, Qwen2-VL, and qualitative displays are added. Existing hyperparameter plots are enlarged and relocated to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v1 supports acceleration mainly through token-retention proxies. v2 resolves this important evidence gap with measured prefilling latency including segmentation and compression overhead, plus explicit FLOP accounting in Table 3. Newline-matched controls, reproduction details, and explicit limitations further strengthen assessment of the central claim. Although some PruneVID comparisons and medium-subset scores are lost, the added evidence substantially improves the paper's overall quality.
